sentence_stem: Had she known about the delay,
correct_completion: she would have taken an earlier train.
full_sentence: Had she known about the delay, she would have taken an earlier train.
acceptable_variants: she would have caught an earlier train.
she might have left the house sooner.

options.text: she takes an earlier train every day.
options.why_wrong: This is a present habit. The stem sets up an unreal past condition, so the completion must refer to the past.

options.text: so she took the earlier train anyway.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a real result, not a hypothetical one. The inverted 'Had she known' requires a conditional main clause.

options.text: she would have taken an earlier train.
she will take an earlier train tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: A future form does not match an unreal past condition. The main clause needs 'would have' plus a past participle.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle)
explanation: The stem is an inverted third conditional: 'Had she known' replaces 'If she had known'. The main clause therefore needs 'would have' plus a past participle to describe an unreal past result. Ukrainian speakers may find this pattern harder to produce because Ukrainian expresses the same unreal past with a single conditional form, so the 'would have' plus past participle structure needs deliberate practice.
